text:
Maya: Heads-up — ran a 1% canary for q2-small-int8 vs prod-stable on the en/zh chat+summarize workloads. Quick summary:
Maya: - p95 latency +18ms overall
Maya: - token cost down ~22%
Maya: - primary ROUGE-L mean -0.9 pts (prod 34.5 -> q2 33.6)
Maya: - hallucination rate +1.8% (absolute) on the grounded-span measure
Maya: - short-completion A/B uplift: -0.4% (not statistically significant)

Juan: Can you paste the per-route numbers?
Maya: Sure, pasted the highlights below:
```yaml
routes:
  chat:
    p95_latency_ms: {prod: 82, q2: 100}
    rouge_l: {prod: 34.5, q2: 33.6}
  summarize:
    p95_latency_ms: {prod: 120, q2: 135}
    rouge_l: {prod: 45.1, q2: 44.4}
  retrieval:
    p95_latency_ms: {prod: 210, q2: 225}
    exact_match: {prod: 78.4, q2: 77.9}
```

Sasha: Hallucination +1.8% — how are we measuring that exactly?
Maya: Using the eval harness (eval-2026-01) — grounded-span precision on curated long-form prompts; we also check span overlap and hallucination tags. The lift is concentrated on >512 token outputs.
Samir: Is this within our canary gates? I thought auto-fallback triggers at >1% absolute hallucination increase.
Maya: Current gate config (prod):
```json
{"gate":"hallucination_abs","threshold":1.0,"window_minutes":60}
```
Maya: So the canary crossed that. Deploy-bot auto-rolled back traffic to 0% because eval-guard-03 fired.

deploy-bot: Canary auto-fallback executed (rule id: eval-guard-03) — traffic reverted to prod-stable.

Juan: Wait — we rolled automatically? Who owns the auto-fallback rule?
Sasha: Is the delta robust or a fluke? Per-seed variance?
Maya: There's variance by language and seed. zh shows larger variance. Raw table uploaded: https://rbx.internal/evals/q2-int8-canary (link).
Samir: Proposal to proceed more safely: keep int8 behind a reduced canary, enable prefix/KV cache for chat route, and run two mitigation arms: int8+cache and int8+quant-stability (extra dequant smoothing). Also stratify seeds by lang/length.
Juan: Also suggest adding a user-visible correctness gate using the client QA set (we've seen ROUGE sometimes miss user-facing regressions).
Maya: Agreed. Drafted new gate suggestions:
```yaml
gates:
  - name: hallucination_abs
    threshold: 1.5   # relax slightly for int8 smoke
    compare_to: prod
  - name: primary_rouge_delta
    threshold_pct: -1.5
  - name: client_qa_pass_rate
    threshold: 0.5  # no more than 0.5% drop
```

Sasha: Can we also cap p95 latency delta? If p95 > +50ms we should throttle.
Samir: Ordering I propose:
1) run 5% AB for 24h (split across lang/length buckets)
2) enable prefix-cache on chat for the experimental variant
3) monitor hallucination_abs, primary_rouge_delta, client_qa_pass_rate, p95_latency
4) auto-rollback if any gate breaches for >30m

Maya: I'll update the rollout config and re-run the smaller AB tomorrow 09:00 PT. @ops-oncall please review the rollback window and alert thresholds.
ops-oncall: ack. I'll create an alert: hallucination_delta > 1.2 (5m) and p95_latency_delta > 60ms. I'll also watch traces for tokenization regressions.
Juan: If we see p95 > 200ms suddenly, we should have a throttling policy to reduce burst size (circuit-breaker).
Maya: Noted. I'll add a canary-specific circuit-breaker rule in the rollout YAML:
```yaml
circuit_breakers:
  - metric: p95_latency_ms
    threshold: 200
    action: throttle
```

Sasha: One more ask — add per-seed breakdown to the canary dashboard and include a 95% bootstrap CI for quality metrics. That will avoid noisy auto-falls.
Samir: Agree. Also run an int4 micro-experiment in parallel but behind a hard stop (manual ramp) — int4 often looks better cost-wise but higher hallucination risk.
Maya: Good call. Plan: 5% int8+cache, 2% int4 manual, run 24h, seeds stratified. If gates pass, ramp to 20% then 50% over 48h. If hallucination_delta > 1.5 or client_qa_drop > 0.5% => immediate rollback.
Juan: Sounds solid. Thanks Maya — please paste the updated rollout YAML here when ready so we can review before scheduling.
Maya: Will do. I'll also attach the raw eval CSV and a short note explaining the zh variance.
Sasha: thx. Small ask — add a note in the runbook about how deploy-bot handles metric name changes (we previously had a false rollback when metric path changed).
Maya: Will update runbook. Scheduling the canary and pinging infra for extra logging retention.
ops-oncall: I'll be on watch at 09:00 PT. Ping me if anything noisy appears.
Maya: Thanks all — closing the loop here. I'll post the updated config once it's uploaded. :thumbsup:
